sources.title: Human History Map civilization index
sources.note: Exact Surasena identity, approximate 500 to 400 BCE interval, generated label and distinct neighboring records.

sources.title: Human History Map 700 BCE borders
sources.note: Decoded broad Vedic Indo-Aryans context layer and target absence before the indexed Surasena interval.

sources.title: Human History Map 500 BCE borders
sources.note: Decoded exact Surasena polygon, topology, coordinate hash, point tests and simultaneous neighboring layers.

sources.title: Human History Map 400 BCE borders
sources.note: Decoded disappearance of exact Surasena and replacement by a broad generic Hindu Kingdoms layer around Mathura.

sources.title: Human History Map 323 BCE borders
sources.note: Decoded later Magadha coverage at the audited Mathura-region points.

sources.title: Human History Map 300 BCE borders
sources.note: Decoded Maurya Empire coverage across the audited Mathura-region points.

sources.title: A. D. H. Bivar, The Indus Lands, Cambridge Ancient History
sources.note: Cambridge synthesis placing Surasena and Mathura within the competitive northern political landscape before Mauryan expansion.

sources.title: University of Delhi, History of India from Earliest Times up to c. 300 CE
sources.note: University teaching volume on Surasena, Mathura, clans, political organization, routes and the limits of later Krishna traditions.

sources.title: INFLIBNET, Mahajanapadas and the Rise of Magadha
sources.note: University module on territorial states, monarchies and oligarchies, agriculture, taxation, armies and northern competition.

sources.title: NIOS, From Janapadas to Empire
sources.note: National Institute of Open Schooling survey of janapadas, farming, iron, routes, cities, revenue and armed forces.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India, Indian Archaeology 1975-76: A Review
sources.note: Official Mathura excavation summary for the sixth through fourth centuries BCE, including floors, postholes, pottery and small finds.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India, Indian Archaeology 1976-77: A Review
sources.note: Official continuation of Mathura excavation reporting, stratigraphic periods, structural change and later early-historic urban material.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India, Indian Archaeology 1966-67: A Review
sources.note: Official first-season summary of the Sonkh excavation, mound location, scale and deep multi-period sequence southwest of Mathura.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India, Indian Archaeology Today: Sonkh
sources.note: Officially digitized archaeological synthesis of Sonkh settlement layers, early pottery, hearths, houses, defenses and later cult buildings.

sources.title: P. A. Eltsov, The Ancient Indian City and the Thought Expressed in It
sources.note: Peer-reviewed reassessment of Mathura settlement, mud defenses, ring wells, drains and major urban change mainly after the target interval.

sources.title: Shonaleeka Kaul, Early Mathura: Sacred Imagination and Diverse Traditions
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study separating strong archaeological evidence for several Mathura traditions from later Krishna-centered literary memory.

sources.title: INFLIBNET, Iron and Urbanization
sources.note: University archaeology module on early historic farming, settlement growth, iron technologies, pottery, crafts and exchange.

sources.title: INFLIBNET, Iron Age Society and Economy
sources.note: University archaeology module on tools, specialized crafts, ceramic manufacture, mixed subsistence and social interpretation.

sources.title: NIOS, The Vedic Age
sources.note: National Institute of Open Schooling background used cautiously for households, hierarchy, women, food and education.

sources.title: NIOS, Ancient India Culture and Heritage
sources.note: National Institute of Open Schooling synthesis of homes, foods, clothing, ornaments, occupations, animals, crafts and play.

sources.title: NIOS, Education, Science and Technology, Medicine
sources.note: National Institute of Open Schooling overview of oral learning, teacher-pupil education and the long development of medicine.

sources.title: UNESCO, Tradition of Vedic chanting
sources.note: Authoritative account of childhood training, tonal accents, recitation techniques and oral preservation.

sources.title: B. V. Subbarayappa, Physicians of ancient India
sources.note: Peer-reviewed medical history distinguishing early healing practices and Buddhist physicians from later compiled Ayurvedic texts.

sources.title: SuttaCentral, Madhura Sutta, Majjhima Nikaya 84, Pali root text
sources.note: Digital canonical Pali text locating Mahakaccana near Madhura and recording a discussion with King Avantiputta.

sources.title: SuttaCentral, Madhura Sutta, Majjhima Nikaya 84, English translation
sources.note: Modern scholarly translation of the Madhura discussion about social rank, wealth, law, service and moral conduct.

sources.title: SuttaCentral, Madhura Sutta, Anguttara Nikaya 5.220, Pali root text
sources.note: Canonical Pali list of five remembered drawbacks of Madhura, including rough ground, dust, dogs and difficult alms.

sources.title: SuttaCentral, Madhura Sutta, Anguttara Nikaya 5.220, English translation
sources.note: Modern translation used to explain the compact Madhura travel complaint and its literary limits.

sources.title: Jamil Ahmed, Sanitation and Waste Management in Ancient India
sources.note: Peer-reviewed historical survey of drains, soakage devices, wells and sanitation evidence, with broad chronological cautions.

sources.title: Heinrich Luders, Mathura Inscriptions
sources.note: Officially digitized epigraphic corpus giving the damaged Mora well inscription, transliteration, language and interpretive context.

sources.title: J. Ph. Vogel, Catalogue of the Archaeological Museum at Mathura
sources.note: Officially digitized museum catalogue locating and describing the Mora well inscription and its archaeological setting.

sources.title: Unicode Consortium, Brahmi code chart
sources.note: Official character chart used to label the displayed Brahmi line as a readable modern Unicode normalization, not a facsimile.

proposedOverrides.summary: A Yamuna janapada around Mathura, preserved through uneven evidence.

batchIdentityNotes: The exact imported id surasena is indexed circa 500 to 400 BCE and was missing both card and override at the initial audit.
The card treats Surasena as a mahajanapada snapshot centered on Mathura and keeps the city longer archaeological and religious history separate.
No appliesTo alias is added. Vedic Indo-Aryans, Kuru, Pancala, Vatsa, Avanti, Magadha, Maurya and generic layers remain distinct.
The sole geometry is one 15-position Polygon with SHA-256 2b048cb2b5325e58621b0cf937ae88cad7094aaed236097da12288707e1e92c2.
The polygon includes Mathura, Vrindavan, Bateshwar and Agra but excludes Sonkh, Govardhan, Bharatpur and Bayana, a material map-history mismatch.
The periods cover only the exact 500 to 400 BCE display window and are evidence lenses rather than invented ruler accessions.
The structured ending is uncertain at 400 BCE. A generic layer immediately follows, while Magadha and Maurya appear only in later snapshots.
The writing sample is the later Mora well inscription, shown in normalized Brahmi Unicode and explicitly separated from Surasena-period speech and writing.
